html:
The Battles of Saratoga were two battles fought on 19 September and 7 October 1777 near Saratoga, in today's New York state. An American army under Horatio Gates stopped a British army under General John Burgoyne, who surrendered on 17 October.

The British plan was to march south from Canada along Lake Champlain and the Hudson River and cut New England off from the other colonies. Burgoyne set out with about 8,000 men. The forests slowed him, his supplies ran short, and the British army in New York sailed for Philadelphia instead of coming north. In the first battle, at Freeman's Farm, he held the field but lost men he could not replace. In the second, at Bemis Heights, the Americans drove him back, led in part by Benedict Arnold. Surrounded by an army now more than twice the size of his own, Burgoyne gave up with about 5,800 men.

It was the turning point of the American Revolutionary War. The victory convinced France that the Americans could win. In February 1778, after talks led by Benjamin Franklin, France signed an alliance with the United States. French money, soldiers and ships made possible the final victory at Yorktown.
